## Personality

Stern, clipped and fair, he barks orders but never mocks a fall. He believes footwork wins more fights than muscle.

## Lore

"Chin up. Eyes front." That is how Quill greets everyone who comes to the Kaldemor Gauntlet, whether they are a nervous recruit, a seasoned adventurer or the mayor. He is forty-nine, lean and upright, with a voice that carries across the whole Park and a habit of standing with his hands clasped behind his back. He is stern, clipped and fair. He barks orders, but he has never once mocked a fall, and he never will. He believes footwork wins more fights than muscle, and he says so roughly forty times a day.

### The road

Quill is not from Kaldemor. He grew up in Selsior, the son of a lamplighter and a laundress, both dead now, and he went out on the Royal Road at twenty-two as a hired guard for the merchant caravans that ran between Selsior and the eastern countryside. He had been on the road two years when the caravan master paired him with a quiet young man from Kaldemor called Hale, on Hale's very first trip.

They rode together for six years. Quill did the shouting and Hale did the watching, and between them they learned to sleep in shifts, to read tracks from a wagon seat and to stand back to back when something came out of the dark beyond the firelight. Each of them is fairly sure he saved the other's life at least once. Quill's version involves a flooded ford, a wolf and Hale standing in the wrong place. Hale's version, which he tells only with a nod, is a different night altogether. They have never agreed, and neither of them would want to.

When Hale went home to be Kaldemor's ranger, Quill stayed on the road for nine more years, as a guard and then as the man who trained the caravans' new guards. It was there that he learned what he knows best: that most people who die on the road die from a bad step, not a weak arm.

### Coming to Kaldemor

Ten years ago Hale wrote to him. It was a short letter, as Hale's letters are. Kaldemor had young people who wanted to fight for the fields and nobody to teach them, and Mayor Tobin would pay. Quill came within the month. He laid out the Gauntlet in the Park himself, and Alfie's carpenters built it to his drawings: the yard where he turns the monsters loose, the hanging course of ropes, logs and platforms that will not wait for anyone, and the ring for the last stand, where a runner must hold out for one full minute. Potions are allowed. Scrolls are not. Fall, flee or run out of time, and it is over, and Quill will send you in again at once.

He and Hale now work a short walk apart, see each other most days, and say very little. It suits them both.

### His recruits

Quill has more recruits this year than ever before, because there are more snails in the meadow than ever before, and he is not sure whether to be proud or worried. He sends no one in until they are seasoned enough to have a chance. He is hardest on the ones he thinks will go farthest. Meg passed the hanging course on her first try, and Quill has never told her she was good, because she already knows. Digby has failed it eleven times. Quill has told him his footwork is improving, which is true, and has quietly lowered nothing, because a course does not care how brave you feel.

Then there is Tam, Wilbur's boy, who hangs on the fence with his stick every afternoon and asks to run the Gauntlet. Quill tells him the same thing every time: when you are bigger. He pretends not to notice the boy watching every run. He does notice, and he shouts his footwork lessons a little louder when Tam is at the fence.

### What he wants and fears

Quill wants every one of his recruits to come home from the meadow on their own two feet. He has buried friends from the road, and he does not intend to bury any from the Gauntlet. What he fears is the day the course stops being practice. Hale kept the thing in the hollow past the woods from him until he knew what it was, and Quill has forgiven him for that, mostly. Since he heard, he has started training the last stand a little longer than one minute.

### Hooks

Quill has quietly begun designing a fourth stage for the Gauntlet, modelled on the Snail King's sweeps, and he needs a traveller who has faced Mano to tell him whether it is fair. Or, one day, Tam will slip under the fence and into the yard, and someone will have to get him out before Quill sees, or after.
